[quote=democratic_sanguivallis;60524267]The man meeting him for now was Don Cirino, who would introduce himself as such. "Cirino Sferrazza, Minister of Commerce.", he tersely replied, making note of Niskala's uncertain tone.

"Strange events seem to be transpiring outside these windows, Mr. Niskala... I, er... I have not been well-informed of events, and while I would really wish to resume the discussions I've had with your government earlier, that doesn't seem to feasible if it means we're supposed to just ignore the massive elephant in the room here..."

Don Cirino then turned to some of the men guarding his person at the back of the room, a four-man team of private personnel under MROS Dynamics, though they would conceal their corporate identity, instead donning the official insignia of the Sanguinian Armed Forces. Among them, Ulf de Mayne would be most prominent, exchange glances with Don Cirino every so often.

"Ahem..." Don Cirino then coughed, looking back at Mr. Niskala. "I'll keep things brief and speak candidly then, Mr. Niskala. What is going on out there?..."[/quote]
Mr. Niskala gave a quick glance to the windows, as if worried that something in the bushes was going to jump at him from outside. He looked back at Cirino and answered, There was a number of occurrences at Ivon involving factory workers and farmers. They had rifles and were being very destructive, so the police handled the situation in the only way they could at that point.

His voice was grim but stern, shifting from his initial shock upon entering the room. The far-left arent taking it well, Ill say that much. I will not be the first to admit that communism has very rarely come to a nation peacefully. I suppose Sanguivallis is the exception, but there is not a chance that Gythena is going to be the same.

I do, however, hope that you will be open to negotiating in these chambers? I dont think Polijamsa has been affected as hard as Ivon or the Maarja Isles.

[quote=the_crystalline_empire;60524309]I perceive your discomfort, Mr. lo Pilato, stated the duchess, If it eases you and madame Terrasi, you may call me comrade Lorraine, she continued.

Rochambeau coughed slightly, but said nothing as Villiard grinned, at the clear evidence of a win on the side of the Montfleur Communists.

Now, let us begin, I should wish that we drop the formalities, and get to the nitty gritty, said the duchess, Lay out your offers,[/quote]
"Don't worry about me then, I'm just here as per the request of the Socialist International." Lo Pilato says, stepping back and letting Terrasi take center stage, which she does, theatrically strutting towards the center of the room.

"Well, well!" Terrasi began, almost teeming with excitement as she was finally allowed to do her job. "Let's begin with a few observations and counterfactuals. I was reading through the past documents we've arranged with the Montfleurois in the past, namely the Treaty of Ipso in 1991 and the Cross-Straits Economic Agreement during the turn of the millennium. CSEC in particular has been a very good boon for the Sanguinian and Montfleurois economies considering the sheer amount of SMEs it helped start up in the digital sector. That said, the lines of credit we prepared for our economic arrangements have been drying up in recent years. Probably all of you would be familiar by now with the economic woes we ran into two years ago. We're here because we wanted to assure this government that those things have long since passed and that Sanguivallis is, once more, open up to business with the anti-fascist world. But we'll have to make revisions to our arrangements to 1) account for the new Sanguinian currency, which currently operates at floated rates compared to the old aurum 2) fine-tune preexisting industrial partnerships to account for the recent spate of nationalizations currently taking place in the Sanguinian market economy, and 3) ensure that we're committed to an environmental policy of Catholic stewardship done in opposition to the rigorous, profit-driven growth of the EDU."

"The second is of particular concern to us." Lo Pilato added. "At the moment, international confidence in Sanguinian industry and services is rather low, and it's easy to understand why. When the revolution happened, we had to nationalize a huge number of industries whose growth had hinged upon heavy borrowing from foreign creditors. When these were nationalized, their liabilities were thrown into the hands of foreign creditors while those responsible for the mess got off scot-free."

"Blah, blah, blah, anyways now is the finest time for partnership to resume as normal!" Terrasi says, cutting off Lo Pilato before he made any more thinly-veiled attempts to undermine the necessity of capitalism. "As of last count, Montfleur and Sanguivallis had about 48 billion something Vespurian dollars in goods traded just before the financial crisis. On the Sanguinian side, most of our exports to your nation had been contributions from our steelworks, like taps and fittings, automotive components, refrigerators, fiber optics, all that kind of stuff. We see this in the partnerships too that our countries have been forming. Sangfe S.p.A.'s acquisition of MGC Industries is one case for example indicative of our close proximity in manufacturing. That said, we are now in a new economic reality. Sangfe, Somare, CNZ, RapidaSol, all of these corporations are now intricately tied to the fate of the Social Renaissance Party, meaning that fundamentally, any partnership done between the Montfleurois and the Sanguinians cannot be viewed anymore as actions of a rational market but as actions of a geopolitical character. Since the final goal of our respective societies is the transition to socialism...-"

"Communism." Lo Pilato corrected.

"Right. Erm, communism... we may as well acknowledge the reality of our situation and foster closer strategic ties with Montfleur [i]in addition[/i] to preexisting economic arrangements. Consultative forums for our respective ministries of commerce is an obvious thing, but this can go further towards say, law enforcement against smuggling and illegal trade that subvert Sanguino-Montfleurois customs and rules of origin agreements. Maybe even a military alliance and a common security program to make our respective economies more resilient against shocks instigated by the EDU, especially any attacks they might prosecute against our network of preexisting industrial alliances."

The duchess listened silently, nodding as she recognized the named treaties and matters, before quipping, It sounds awfully capitalist of you, she laughed and then continued, Indeed, these matters are extensive in their nature, and of course none of the old treaties have been declared void yet, so the matter still stands. Of course we are bastions it seems of good taste and faith on this continent, so I would seek to bring this matter before the assembly, she stated.

As she finished speaking the doors of the sitting room would open, and the king of Montfleur entered.

The king was a stunning sight of beauty, youthful, slim, and crowned by blonde curls which danced down his head and onto his shoulders, a slight smile lay upon his face, not approving, nor disapproving.

I apologise for my lateness duchess, began the king, bowing as he turned to bow also to the guests.

The duchess nodded as he sat down, his curls bouncing, I assume the boring details are done? Enquired the king.
We were just discussing them, replied the duchess.

Ah, well, just say yes to them, they are excellent for trade, especially in such a volatile place like Elseyr, the EDU is a constant pressing force on the southeast of this continent, he said with a wave of his hand.

"Boring?!" Terrasi loudly exclaimed, completely forgetting that they were talking to the King of Montfleur himself. "Economics is the coolest thing ever, it's what gives life to-..."

"Your Majesty." Lo Pilato says suddenly, cutting off Terrasi, his face cringing once again as he acknowledged yet another noble title in an attempt to prevent his advisor from becoming persona non grata. "And yes, the EDU has been a problem in recent times. They are neo-imperialists, fascists wearing the veil of liberal democracy, who takes from the poor to fill the bellies of the rich, exploitative against the worker, degenerate and decadent. It's actually one of the driving reasons why we decided to approach you today."

"I thought we were here for trade?"

"Comrade Terrasi, check the wallpaper of the room for a second, it looks really nice. I'd like to take inspiration from it for renovations in the Palazzo."

"Ooh, gotcha!" Terrasi enthusiastically says, suddenly turning away from the conversation.

"Comrade Lorraine, Your Majesty." Lo Pilato began. "We are faced with a crisis the likes of which has never been seen before. That crisis is of the fate of the communist revolution all over. I have spoken at length about this with Comrade Rochambeau, and now I shall speak this again with you. The minimum program of subjugating the proletariat with social benefits is good in a utilitarian sense, but it brings no liberation to the masses. It is the feeding of birds in cages, a constriction on the right of man to live to the highest levels that could be accorded to them by a communist society. What Comrade Terrasi has told us about economic partnerships is true, but we have to look beyond these simple pursuits of human happiness and understand that our respective regimes will soon be targets by the liberal international order. It is for this reason that I extend my hand to the Montfleurois government to adopt a more orthodox political line, to adhere to the vanguardist principles of the Socialist International and its recommended praxis, for your salvation and for all mankind."
